rows.group: Tax on the sale price
rows.label: City transfer tax, base rate
rows.quote: The present tax (“Base Tax”) is computed based on the consideration or value of the real property interest conveyed at a rate of 0.45%. The special tax under Measure ULA (“ULA Tax”) imposes an additional tax on top of the Base Tax.

rows.group: Tax on the sale price
rows.label: City base rate expressed per $500
rows.value: $2.25 per $500 or part thereof
rows.quote: The Base Tax rate of $2.25 per $500 or part thereof (“Base Rate”).

rows.group: Tax on the sale price
rows.label: Sale prices at which the Measure ULA tax starts
rows.quote: Note: Effective for transactions closing after June 30, 2026, the new ULA thresholds will be $5,400,000 and $10,900,000. Transactions greater than $5,400,000 but less than $10,900,000 will be assessed a 4% tax, and transactions of $10,900,000 or greater will be assessed a 5.5% tax.

rows.group: Tax on the sale price
rows.label: Measure ULA rate, sale price above $5,400,000 and below $10,900,000
rows.quote: Transactions greater than $5,400,000 but less than $10,900,000 will be assessed a 4% tax, and transactions of $10,900,000 or greater will be assessed a 5.5% tax.

rows.group: Tax on the sale price
rows.label: Measure ULA rate, sale price of $10,900,000 or more
rows.quote: Transactions greater than $5,400,000 but less than $10,900,000 will be assessed a 4% tax, and transactions of $10,900,000 or greater will be assessed a 5.5% tax.

rows.group: Tax on the sale price
rows.label: Total city rate at or below $5,400,000
rows.quote: Value of Property Conveyed | Base Rate* | ULA Rate | Applicable Tax Rate | > $100; ≤ $5,400,000 | $2.25 / $500 | 0% | 0.45%*

rows.group: Tax on the sale price
rows.label: Total city rate above $5,400,000 and below $10,900,000
rows.quote: Value of Property Conveyed | Base Rate* | ULA Rate | Applicable Tax Rate | > $5,400,000;<$10,900,000 | $2.25 / $500 | 4% | 4.45%*

rows.group: Tax on the sale price
rows.label: Total city rate at $10,900,000 or more
rows.quote: Value of Property Conveyed | Base Rate* | ULA Rate | Applicable Tax Rate | ≥ $10,900,000 | $2.25 / $500 | 5.5% | 5.95%*

rows.group: Tax on the sale price
rows.label: What the city tax is charged on
rows.value: The consideration or value of the real property interest conveyed
rows.quote: The real property transfer tax is an excise tax on the privilege of selling a real property interest, not a tax on the property itself, and is calculated on the consideration or value of the real property interest conveyed.

rows.group: Tax on the sale price
rows.label: How the thresholds move
rows.value: Adjusted annually based on the Bureau of Labor Statistics Chained Consumer Price Index
rows.quote: Consistent with the Measure ULA, the value thresholds of when to apply the ULA Tax and its corresponding rates are adjusted annually based on the Bureau of Labor Statistics Chained Consumer Price Index.

rows.group: Tax on the sale price
rows.label: Date the Measure ULA tax took effect
rows.value: April 1, 2023
rows.quote: The ULA Tax is applicable to qualified conveyances of real property interests that occur on or after April 1, 2023.

rows.group: Tax on the sale price
rows.label: County transfer tax
rows.value: $0.55 for each $500 or fractional part
rows.quote: when the consideration or value of the interest or property conveyed (exclusive of the value of any lien or encumbrance remaining thereon at the time of sale) exceeds one hundred dollars ($100) a tax at the rate of fifty-five cents ($0.55) for each five hundred dollars ($500) or fractional part thereof.
rows.note: The statute authorises counties to impose this rate. That Los Angeles County has done so, and collects the city tax at recording, should be confirmed on the Registrar-Recorder's fee page before closing; see the Flagged for Review page.

rows.group: Tax on the sale price
rows.label: County transfer tax as a percentage

rows.group: Tax on the sale price
rows.label: What the county tax is charged on
rows.value: Consideration or value conveyed, exclusive of any lien or encumbrance remaining at the time of sale
rows.quote: when the consideration or value of the interest or property conveyed (exclusive of the value of any lien or encumbrance remaining thereon at the time of sale) exceeds one hundred dollars ($100)

rows.group: Tax on the sale price
rows.label: City plus county transfer tax, sale at or below $5,400,000

calc.formula: City rate (0.45%) plus county rate ($0.55 per $500)

rows.group: Tax on the sale price
rows.label: City plus county transfer tax, sale above $5,400,000 and below $10,900,000
rows.note: The tax applies to the whole price once the threshold is passed, not only to the part above it: the FAQ's example table shows a single 'Applicable Tax Rate' for each value band.

calc.formula: City rate (4.45%) plus county rate ($0.55 per $500)

rows.group: Tax on the sale price
rows.label: Extra tax triggered by crossing $5,400,000 by one dollar
rows.note: A price just above the threshold nets less than a price just below it. Whether the subject is anywhere near this price is unknown because its rent and value are unknown.

rows.group: Property tax while the property is held
rows.label: Largest yearly rise in assessed value
rows.value: 2 percent
rows.quote: (b) The full cash value base may reflect from year to year the inflationary rate not to exceed 2 percent for any given year or reduction as shown in the consumer price index or comparable data for the area under taxing jurisdiction, or may be reduced to reflect substantial damage, destruction, or other factors causing a decline in value.

rows.group: Property tax while the property is held
rows.label: Basic tax rate
rows.value: 1% of assessed value, plus bonded indebtedness and direct assessment taxes
rows.quote: As a result, the maximum levy cannot exceed 1% of a property’s assessed value (plus bonded indebtedness and direct assessment taxes). Increases in assessed value are limited to 2% annually except when property changes of ownership or undergoes new construction.

rows.group: Property tax while the property is held
rows.label: When a property is reassessed to market value
rows.value: Only upon a change in ownership or completion of new construction
rows.quote: In contrast, under Proposition 13, properties are reassessed to current market value only upon a change in ownership or completion of new construction (called the base year value).

rows.group: Property tax while the property is held
rows.label: What a sale does to the buyer's property tax
rows.value: Reappraisal as of the recording date of the deed
rows.quote: When a publicly recorded transfer occurs, the Assessor receives a copy of the deed and determines whether a reappraisal is required under State law. The date of reappraisal is generally the recording date of the deed that transfers ownership.
rows.note: Under a net lease the tenant usually pays property tax, so a buyer's reassessment raises the tenant's occupancy cost. Whether that is so here depends on the lease (row PL-017).

rows.group: Property tax while the property is held
rows.label: Date of reassessment when property is inherited
rows.value: The date of death of the property owner
rows.quote: However, the reappraisal of property acquired by inheritance from an estate or living trust occurs as of the date of death of the property owner, not as of the date of distribution to the beneficiary.

rows.group: Property tax while the property is held
rows.label: Passing a property other than a principal residence to children
rows.value: Proposition 19 eliminates exclusion for other real property other than the principal residence
rows.quote: Other Real Property | Proposition 58/193 (Former Law): Transferor lifetime limit of $1,000,000 of factored base year value | Proposition 19 (Current Law): Eliminates exclusion for other real property other than the principal residence | Important Dates | Through February 15, 2021 | Effective February 16, 2021
rows.note: Heirs receive a stepped-up income-tax basis (row TX-046) but the property is reassessed to market value for property tax.

rows.group: Property tax while the property is held
rows.label: Earthquake retrofit work
rows.value: Not treated as new construction
rows.quote: For purposes of this section, the term “newly constructed” does not include that portion of an existing structure that consists of the construction or reconstruction of seismic retrofitting components, as defined by the Legislature.

rows.group: Property tax while the property is held
rows.label: Rebuilding after a disaster declared by the Governor
rows.value: Not treated as new construction where the rebuilt value is comparable
rows.quote: For purposes of this section, “newly constructed” does not include real property that is reconstructed after a disaster, as declared by the Governor, where the fair market value of the real property, as reconstructed, is comparable to its fair market value prior to the disaster.

rows.group: Property tax while the property is held
rows.label: Moving the assessed value to a replacement property after a disaster
rows.value: Allowed within the same county for property substantially damaged or destroyed
rows.quote: (e) (1) Notwithstanding any other provision of this section, the Legislature shall provide that the base year value of property that is substantially damaged or destroyed by a disaster, as declared by the Governor, may be transferred to comparable property within the same county that is acquired or newly constructed as a replacement for the substantially damaged or destroyed property.

rows.group: Property tax while the property is held
rows.label: What counts as substantially damaged
rows.value: Physical damage of more than 50 percent of value
rows.quote: (f) For the purposes of subdivision (e): (1) Property is substantially damaged or destroyed if it sustains physical damage amounting to more than 50 percent of its value immediately before the disaster. Damage includes a diminution in the value of property as a result of restricted access caused by the disaster.

rows.group: Property tax while the property is held
rows.label: Assessed value may fall after damage
rows.value: May be reduced to reflect substantial damage, destruction or other decline in value
rows.quote: (b) The full cash value base may reflect from year to year the inflationary rate not to exceed 2 percent for any given year [...] or may be reduced to reflect substantial damage, destruction, or other factors causing a decline in value.

rows.group: Income tax on a gain from sale
rows.label: Top federal rate on most long-term capital gain
rows.quote: However, a capital gains rate of 20% applies to the extent that your taxable income exceeds the thresholds set for the 15% capital gain rate.

rows.group: Income tax on a gain from sale
rows.label: Taxable income above which the 20% rate applies
rows.value: $533,400 single; $600,050 married filing jointly
rows.quote: A capital gains rate of 15% applies if your taxable income is: more than $48,350 but less than or equal to $533,400 for single; [...] more than $96,700 but less than or equal to $600,050 for married filing jointly and qualifying surviving spouse;

rows.group: Income tax on a gain from sale
rows.label: Top federal rate on gain attributable to past depreciation of real property
rows.quote: The portion of any unrecaptured section 1250 gain from selling section 1250 real property is taxed at a maximum 25% rate.

rows.group: Income tax on a gain from sale
rows.label: Federal net investment income tax
rows.value: 3.8 percent
rows.quote: A 3.8 percent net investment income tax (NIIT) applies to individuals, estates, and trusts that have net investment income above applicable threshold amounts.

rows.group: Income tax on a gain from sale
rows.label: Income above which the net investment income tax applies
rows.value: $250,000 married filing jointly; $200,000 single
rows.quote: the excess of modified adjusted gross income (MAGI) over the following threshold amounts: $250,000 for married filing jointly or qualifying surviving spouse | $125,000 for married filing separately | $200,000 for single or head of household

rows.group: Income tax on a gain from sale
rows.label: Whether that tax reaches rents and gains on real estate
rows.value: Yes: rents and net gains from real estate, unless from a trade or business the tax does not cover
rows.quote: interest, dividends, certain annuities, royalties, and rents (unless derived in a trade or business in which the NIIT doesn't apply), [...] net gains from the disposition of property such as stocks, bonds, mutual funds, and real estate (to the extent taken into account in computing taxable income), other than property held in a trade or business to which NIIT doesn't apply

rows.group: Income tax on a gain from sale
rows.label: Top California rate in the 2025 schedules
rows.value: 12.30%, above $742,953 single or $1,485,906 married filing jointly
rows.quote: Schedule X - Single or Married/RDP Filing Separately | 742,953 | AND OVER | 72,219.84 + 12.30% | Schedule Y - Married/RDP Filing Jointly | 1,485,906 | AND OVER | 144,439.65 + 12.30%

rows.group: Income tax on a gain from sale
rows.label: California rate across the widest band

rows.group: Income tax on a gain from sale
rows.label: Highest combined federal rate on long-term gain
rows.note: Top of the range, before state tax. The owner's actual rate depends on income, filing status, basis and depreciation taken, none of which is known to this workbook.

calc.formula: Top long-term capital gain rate (20%) plus net investment income tax (3.8%)

rows.group: Deferring or removing the tax on a gain
rows.label: Exchange into other real property
rows.value: Generally no gain or loss recognised on a like-kind exchange
rows.quote: Generally, if you make a like-kind exchange, you are not required to recognize a gain or loss under Internal Revenue Code Section 1031.

rows.group: Deferring or removing the tax on a gain
rows.label: Cash or other property taken out of an exchange
rows.value: Gain recognised to the extent of the other property and money received
rows.quote: If, as part of the exchange, you also receive other (not like-kind) property or money, you must recognize a gain to the extent of the other property and money received. You can’t recognize a loss.

rows.group: Deferring or removing the tax on a gain
rows.label: What kinds of property qualify
rows.value: Real property only; improved or unimproved real property is generally like-kind
rows.quote: Under the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act, Section 1031 now applies only to exchanges of real property and not to exchanges of personal or intangible property. [...] Real properties generally are of like-kind, regardless of whether they’re improved or unimproved.

rows.group: Deferring or removing the tax on a gain
rows.label: Replacement property outside the United States
rows.value: Not like-kind
rows.quote: However, real property in the United States is not like-kind to real property outside the United States.

rows.group: Deferring or removing the tax on a gain
rows.label: Time allowed to name the replacement property
rows.value: 45 days
rows.quote: The replacement property for the exchange must be identified within 45 days after the property being given up is transferred. The replacement property must be received within 180 days, or by the due date of your tax return (including extensions), whichever is earlier.

rows.group: Deferring or removing the tax on a gain
rows.label: Time allowed to receive the replacement property
rows.value: 180 days, or the due date of the tax return (including extensions), whichever is earlier
rows.quote: The replacement property for the exchange must be identified within 45 days after the property being given up is transferred. The replacement property must be received within 180 days, or by the due date of your tax return (including extensions), whichever is earlier.

rows.group: Deferring or removing the tax on a gain
rows.label: If the timing requirements are missed
rows.value: Any gain may be taxable in the year the property was transferred
rows.quote: If you fail to meet the timing requirements because of the QI, your transaction won't qualify as a deferred exchange and any gain may be taxable in the year you transferred the property.

rows.group: Deferring or removing the tax on a gain
rows.label: Who may not act as the intermediary
rows.value: Related parties and agents of the taxpayer
rows.quote: Related parties and agents of the taxpayer aren’t eligible to be QIs, and are referred to as “disqualified persons.”

rows.group: Deferring or removing the tax on a gain
rows.label: Whether an interest in a partnership or a certificate of trust qualifies as replacement property
rows.value: No: never real property for this purpose
rows.quote: The following assets are exceptions and not real property for purposes of section 1031, regardless of the classification of the property under state or local law. Stock [...], bonds, or notes. Other securities or evidences of indebtedness or interest. Interests in a partnership (other than an interest in a partnership that has in effect a valid election under section 761(a) [...]). Certificates of trust or beneficial interests.
rows.note: Matters when a seller is offered a pooled or fractional replacement product: its legal form decides whether it qualifies. Needs the owner's tax adviser.

rows.group: Deferring or removing the tax on a gain
rows.label: Tax basis of inherited property
rows.value: Generally the fair market value on the date of the decedent's death
rows.quote: The basis of property inherited from a decedent is generally one of the following: The fair market value (FMV) of the property on the date of the decedent's death (whether or not the executor of the estate files an estate tax return [...]). The FMV of the property on the alternate valuation date, but only if the executor of the estate files an estate tax return (Form 706) and elects to use the alternate valuation on that return.
rows.note: Holding until death can remove the income tax on gain built up during the owner's life; selling during life does not. This is one of the largest differences between the hold and sell paths and depends on the owner's estate plan (row PL-043).

rows.group: Income tax on a gain from sale
rows.label: Additional California tax on taxable income above $1,000,000
rows.value: 1 percent
rows.quote: (a) For each taxable year beginning on or after January 1, 2005, in addition to any other taxes imposed by this part, an additional tax shall be imposed at the rate of 1 percent on that portion of a taxpayer’s taxable income in excess of one million dollars ($1,000,000).

rows.group: Income tax on a gain from sale
rows.label: Highest California rate including the additional 1 percent
rows.note: California taxes capital gain at the same rates as other income; it has no separate lower rate in the schedules read. Top of the range only.

calc.formula: Top schedule rate (12.30%) plus additional tax on income above $1,000,000 (1%)
